name: DIAGNOSTIC - 05 formation flying, constant_thrust plus eclipse model present
description:
Fourth diagnostic scenario, NOT a permanent template. Findings so far: no force effector at all -> clean. constant_thrust alone (no eclipse reading, since ConstantFrameThrustController has no eclipse message reader at all) -> clean. station_keeping ALONE (no phasing_keeping, no sharing/arbitration) -> CRASHES at the identical point, ruling out the two-controller-sharing-one-effector mechanism.

The one remaining difference between the clean constant_thrust diagnostic and the crashing station_keeping-alone one: station_keeping reads an eclipse message every tick (self.eclipseInMsg.isLinked() / .shadowFactor) for its eclipse-gated reboost; constant_thrust does not (and, since constant_thrust does not trigger engine.service.build()'s needs_eclipse condition, the shared Eclipse() model was never even built in that earlier diagnostic).

This scenario isolates whether the mere PRESENCE of the eclipse model/machinery is the trigger, independent of whether our own controller reads it: follower-1 has ONLY constant_thrust configured (same as before -- no eclipse reading, same as the clean diagnostic), but ALSO has enable_srp=True, which forces engine.service.build()'s needs_eclipse condition true and builds the real shared Eclipse() model/SRP effector, exactly as station_keeping does -- just without constant_thrust itself ever reading eclipseInMsg.

If this crashes, the Eclipse()/SRP machinery itself is implicated, independent of which controller reads it. If it does NOT crash, that points specifically at station_keeping's/phasing_keeping's own act of READING eclipseInMsg.isLinked()/.shadowFactor from within their UpdateState() callback as the trigger.
